sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the clip describes construction of a tagged full-length characterization construct but reports no specific trafficking, surface-expression, or functional assay result.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names residue 29 as the HA-tag insertion site in a full-length NRN1 construct. The signal peptide ends at residue 27 (A) and the mature N-terminus begins at residue 28 (A); 'HA-tag at residue 29' is interpreted as the tag inserted after residue 28 and before residue 29, placing it one residue into the extracellular mature protein. NRN1 is GPI-anchored with no transmembrane domain, so the entire mature ectodomain (residues 28–142) is extracellular and the ±1 residue ambiguity does not affect the extracellular classification. Python verification confirms residue 28 = A and residue 29 = G, consistent with the junction reported. Human NRN1 (NM_016588.2) full-length construct with HA tag inserted at residue 29, used for protein characterization (PMC10441612).

sources.claim: Human Neuritin ( NM_016588.2 ) was modified with an HA-tag at residue 29.

literature_notes: NRN1 is a GPI-anchored protein; the topology string shows no TM (M) or intracellular (I) residues — the entire mature protein (residues 28–142) is extracellular. The only ledger line (L1) supports a single near-N-terminal HA-tag site at the junction of residues 28–29. No other insertions, loops, or positions are grounded in the ledger. The C-terminal GPI anchor signal region (approximately residues 121–142) is cleaved in the mature protein and would not be a valid surface-tag site regardless.
